analysis.title: What role can gold play in portfolios? (UBS House View Briefcase)
key_insights: Gold fell back below USD 4,000 an ounce after a stronger-than-expected October US inflation report, rising Treasury yields and a firmer US dollar revived expectations of further Fed tightening.
Gold closed the week around USD 3,880 an ounce, 4.6% lower than where it started the week.
Rising Treasury yields and a firmer dollar raised the opportunity cost of holding gold and reversed its post-election rebound.

UBS expects a faster normalization of energy supply and prices to reinforce its 2027 disinflation outlook and support expectations that major central banks, particularly the Fed, finish raising rates in the first quarter.

UBS expects expectations of lower bond yields and potentially lower policy rates to gain traction once inflation moderates more meaningfully in the second quarter. Until then, elevated real yields and a firm dollar may remain near-term headwinds for gold.
UBS forecasts gold to rise over the next 12 months, supported by central bank buying, reserve diversification, elevated government debt and geopolitical uncertainty.

UBS suggests underallocated investors add gold exposure during price weakness, and that investors with an affinity for real assets consider a mid-single-digit gold allocation within a diversified portfolio.
Q3 total gold demand, including over-the-counter transactions, was 1,369 metric tons, 1% below the prior-year level. Q3 mine production rose 3% y/y to a record 1,071 metric tons.
Gold's sensitivity to real interest rates has weakened, which UBS reads as structural demand providing a stronger offset than in previous cycles.
Strong central bank demand should limit near-term downside in gold.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The hotter print and hawkish Fed commentary revived expectations of further Fed tightening and pressured gold.

macro_indicators.reading: Major central banks, particularly the Fed, finish raising rates in Q1 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: If energy supply and prices normalize faster, the end of tightening would support gold, with lower yields and possibly lower policy rates gaining traction as inflation moderates in Q2.

macro_indicators.reading: USD 3,880 per ounce weekly close, down 4.6% on the week
macro_indicators.interpretation: Gold is below the USD 4,000 threshold.

trade_ideas.description: Long gold: build or maintain a mid-single-digit strategic allocation within a diversified portfolio, adding on price weakness
trade_ideas.rationale: Central bank buying, reserve diversification, elevated government debt and geopolitical uncertainty support gold over 12 months.
trade_ideas.risk: Elevated real yields and a firm US dollar near term, and further Fed tightening.

risk_factors: Further Fed tightening if inflation stays elevated.
Elevated real yields and a firm US dollar.
Energy supply and prices not normalizing, which would delay disinflation.
vol_and_positioning: UBS expects gold to stay volatile near term while inflation remains elevated and markets assess the scope for further Fed tightening.

key_data_points.context: 4.6% lower than the start of the week, week ending 2026-11-13
key_data_points.anchor: The yellow metal closed the week around USD 3,880 an ounce, 4.6% lower than where it started the week

key_data_points.metric: Total Q3 gold demand including OTC
key_data_points.anchor: Total third-quarter gold demand, including over-the-counter transactions, reached 1,369 metric tons, just 1% below the prior-year level.
Mine production rose 3% year over year to a third-quarter record of 1,071 metric tons.

tension_points.bull_case: Central bank buying, ETF inflows, reserve diversification and fiscal concerns provide structural support, and gold's sensitivity to real rates has weakened.
tension_points.bear_case: Stronger US inflation, rising Treasury yields and a firmer dollar revive expectations of further Fed tightening and raise gold's opportunity cost.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy supply and prices failing to normalize and inflation not moderating in Q2, which would keep the Fed tightening beyond Q1.

theme_stances.key_argument: Structural demand from central banks and reserve diversification supports gold over 12 months despite near-term headwinds from real yields and the dollar.
theme_stances.evidence: We remain constructive on gold over the next 12 months
